text:
Marathon Petroleum gained less than 1% today, a modest move that fits into a much larger two-week rally of nearly 9%. The stock has been riding waves of Middle East geopolitical tension — Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its East-West crude pipeline after drone attacks, and Houthi militants advancing toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (a critical chokepoint for global oil shipping) have kept crude prices elevated. US refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, near maximum utilization, which means refiners like Marathon benefit when oil prices stay high and regional supply concerns keep crude in demand.

Today's small dip came on the same day oil prices fell slightly, snapping a multi-day winning streak as markets digested the week's Middle East escalation. But the broader backdrop — geopolitical risk to Middle Eastern supply and near-maximum refinery utilization at home — continues to support refiner margins, which is why the stock has held most of its two-week gains rather than retreating.
